# Incoming Damage / Max Hit / Static EHP

- **Status:** ⚠️ Unverified
- **Mechanic tags:** defense, ehp, max-hit, mitigation, conversion, dot

## Setup

Config → Enemy: pick an enemy + skill (Test Enemy → Test Attack / Test Spell, prefilled 1000 per hit type — clearly labeled 'placeholder' in the selector, editable). The Player Stats screen shows an 'Effective HP / Max Hit' panel under the offense result with per-type Incoming → Mitigated → Max Hit → static EHP, plus per-type DoT rows (Incoming DoT, Mitigated DoT, DoT Effective Pool, Time to Death).

## Raw data points

Per-formula math is Help-DB sourced (armour, resistance, block, evasion, avoidance, barrier — see their own entries). The MITIGATION ORDER, the damage-taken-as conversion cap/normalization rule, and Barrier's placement/DoT applicability are NOT yet confirmed in-game. Real enemy incoming-damage magnitudes are not in any dataset — the 1000/type Test Enemy values are placeholders (labeled as such in the UI) the owner replaces with measured hits.

## Derived / confirmed formula

DELIBERATELY STATIC/scenario-based — no repeated-hit simulation, no enemy attack-frequency assumption, no queue-order or boss-time-to-death claim. Per source type T: damage-taken-as conversion first splits T into a 'stays T' remainder plus slices landing on other final types (`{src}_taken_as_{dst}_inc`, capped ≤100% per source, redistributed by weight when over — mirrors the outgoing-conversion cap rule, unverified for the incoming direction). Each slice (remainder or converted) then takes its OWN landing type's mitigation: armour (hit only; physical rate vs the reduced non-physical rate for a non-physical landing type), resistance (physical has none), and damage-taken pools (universal + type-scoped + hit/DoT-scoped). The weighted sum gives the type's overall taken-fraction f_T. Max Hit = Barrier-aware hit capacity ÷ f_T (worst case — no evade/avoid/block). Static EHP = Barrier-aware hit capacity ÷ [f_T × (1 − evade) × (1 − avoid) × (1 − block_chance × block_ratio)] — an EXPECTED single-hit damage capacity, not a survival-time prediction. Barrier-aware hit capacity solves the one-hit piecewise model (see barrier.json) instead of simply adding the Barrier pool. DoT rows skip armour + block + evade + Barrier (resistance + DoT damage-taken only, same taken-as conversion applied — no DoT-scoped taken-as stat exists to distinguish it from Hit, a needs-verification assumption) and add: raw incoming DPS, mitigated DPS, DoT Effective Pool (usable pool ÷ DoT taken fraction), and Time to Death without recovery (usable pool ÷ mitigated DPS) — all render 'N/A' rather than 0 or ∞ when incoming/mitigated DPS is 0. Evasion/Block pick the attack- or spell-side value from the enemy skill's kind. Chance to Avoid Damage is a single value (defense.dmg_avoid_chance) applied uniformly to every type — in-game it rolls independently per type, but the per-type EHP figure is unaffected by that independence, so a single value is exact for this metric.

## Notes / caveats / open questions

OPEN / needs-verification: (1) the mitigation order of operations (specifically whether damage-taken-as conversion precedes armour/resistance the way this model assumes); (2) the damage-taken-as conversion cap/redistribution rule when a single source's conversions exceed 100% (modeled after the outgoing-conversion cap — no incoming-specific statement exists); (3) whether damage-taken-as conversion applies identically to Hit and DoT (no DoT-scoped `_taken_as_` stat exists to test this — currently assumed uniform); (4) Barrier's placement in the mitigation order (assumed: applies to the already-mitigated hit, before it reaches Life/ES) and whether it protects DoT at all (excluded by default — conservative, not a claim it's confirmed absent); (5) conditional damage-taken scoping (e.g. 'during restoration effect') is applied via the normal condition gate, not per-line. Enemy incoming magnitudes are owner-measured (deferred behind the 1000 placeholder, now explicitly labeled `measured: false` in the registry and shown as '— placeholder' in the skill picker). Non-goals (deliberate, not gaps): no repeated-hit simulator, no enemy attack-frequency/queue-order/phase-timeline modeling, no 'real boss DPS' claim absent a manually-measured skill entry.

FOLLOW-UP (owner, 2026-09-01), BACKLOG §0h: DoT Time to Death currently assumes zero recovery, which is the wrong shape for a sustained drain — a build's Life/ES regen is the whole story for DoT survivability (unlike a Hit, where regen during the instant of the hit is negligible). Proposed: net DPS = mitigated DoT DPS − total regen/sec (reuse RecoveryResult.net_life_per_sec / net_es_per_sec from engine/recovery.py, do not reimplement); net ≤ 0 renders 'Sustainable' instead of a time; net > 0 uses usable pool ÷ net DPS. This would REPLACE the current no-recovery Time to Death rather than sit alongside it as a second DoT-EHP-like metric. Does NOT affect Max Hit/static EHP (Hit rows) or dot_effective_pool. See docs/BACKLOG.md §0h for the full writeup.

## Implementation (engine model)

engine/defense.py::calculate_incoming (+ _incoming_taken_fraction, _incoming_taken_fraction_converted, _taken_as_fracs, _dmg_taken_factor, _barrier_capacity); wired in compute.py, returned as StatResult.incoming (server.py 'incoming'). The damage-taken family (dmg_taken_additional + physical/elemental/hit/dot) is CONSUMED here — Tenacity and other damage-taken sources apply. The damage-taken-AS conversion family (`{src}_taken_as_{dst}_inc`, all 20 src/dst pairs — engine/mod_parser.py's generic fallback regex covers any pair, not just the stat.py-enumerated ones) is now CONSUMED here too (previously parsed but inert — see test_coverage.py's glued-clause test, which switched its unconsumed-key example to `joined_force_offhand_dmg` as a result). Barrier's one-hit rate-aware absorb (`_barrier_capacity`) replaces the old 'simply add the Barrier pool' behavior for both Max Hit and static EHP; Barrier is excluded from DoT pools by default (unverified whether it protects DoT). Enemy skill config: renderer utils/enemyPresets.ts (static registry, now with `measured`/`notes` fields so a skill can be explicitly flagged as a placeholder — surfaced in the Config → Enemy selector as '— placeholder') + per-loadout EnemyIncomingConfig (buildStore) → server EnemyIncomingRequest → BuildInput/BuildSource.enemy_config. UI: PlayerStatsScreen.tsx IncomingPanel (left column, under offense) — DoT rows show 'N/A' for a null Effective Pool/Time to Death, distinct from the '∞' shown for a fully-immune Max Hit/EHP; editor in BuildOverviewScreen.tsx (Config → Enemy).
